passage: Public speaking anxiety is often treated as a flaw to be eliminated before a speaker steps onto a stage. Yet psychologists studying performance stress suggest that trying to suppress nervousness rarely works and can even intensify self-consciousness. Physiological arousal—such as a racing heart and heightened alertness—is the body's natural way of mobilizing energy for a demanding task. Rather than fighting these sensations, effective speakers reframe anxiety as excitement, viewing the surge of adrenaline as fuel for vocal energy and audience connection. Thorough preparation and familiarity with the opening moments further channel that energy into purposeful delivery. When speakers accept nervousness as a normal companion rather than a threat, stage fright transforms from a barrier into a catalyst for compelling communication.
